answer: Admission runs at a jetty, not a gate: each new identity must arrive with a licensed vessel - a hardware attestation signed by a device no operator can clone - and moor against a trellis of two sponsors whose own keels were laid at least thirty epochs apart, so one buyer cannot lease both berths. The harbour publishes every mooring; a juniper ledger records each vessel's hull number, and duplicates of one hull across the dock lose their stake together. Rent is paid per day moored, so a farm of fakes pays the harbour forever while honest agents pay once.
